mainTopic: Ownership rights in a קרבן פסח according to רבי, and slaughtering the פסח for people finishing their purification
overview: The amud opens with אביי. He says that if not for רבי אושעיא, he would have explained the אתנן משנה as being about קדשים קלים, following רבי יוסי הגלילי. In that reading, רבי holds that a person keeps rights only in money set aside for a פסח, not in the animal itself. אביי then sees that the source cannot follow רבי יוסי, so he accepts רבי אושעיא's view: according to רבי, a person keeps some rights even in his פסח animal. The גמרא then quotes the משנה about consecrated animals and birds given as אתנן, along with the two קל וחומר arguments answered by the words 'לכל נדר'. It asks why a פסוק was needed, since a person cannot forbid what is not his. רבי אושעיא answers that the case is registering a זונה on one's פסח, following רבי. Next comes רבי's ברייתא, which says Jews consecrate their פסח on condition that they may register others for money. רבה and רבי זירא then argue about what that money may be spent on. The גמרא also defends אביי by re-reading the condition as applying to the money. Finally, a new משנה rules on when the פסח may be slaughtered for a זב, a זבה, and a שומרת יום כנגד יום, and רב adds that we slaughter for a טבול יום and a מחוסר כפורים.

steps.title: אביי offers a different way to explain the prostitute-payment משנה
steps.stepSummary: אַבָּיֵי says that if רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא had not already explained the משנה as a פסח case following רַבִּי, he would explain it as קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, following רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אַבָּיֵי said: If רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא had not explained that משנה as a case of signing up a זוֹנָה on one's פסח, following רַבִּי, I would have explained it as talking about קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, following רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי. He says that קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים are the owner's property.
steps.whatsHappening: אַבָּיֵי is opening his own explanation of a משנה that רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא already explained differently. This line sets up the reasoning he gives in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes a person can use a consecrated animal as payment, so he must own it in some way. רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא found that ownership in a פסח, following רַבִּי. אַבָּיֵי instead finds it in קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, because רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי openly calls them the owner's money.

keyTerms.meaning: He established / he explained it as referring to a certain case
Signs up a prostitute as a member of his Paschal lamb (as her payment)
Offerings of lesser holiness (e.g., שְׁלָמִים, פסח)
Property of the owners
According to the view of

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אַבָּיֵי is arguing on רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא outright. He says 'אִי לָאו' (if not for). In other words, he respects that explanation but shows another possible one.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּאוֹקְמֵיהּ רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא לְהַהִיא
phrases.english: If not that Rabbi Oshaya established that [Mishnah]
as a case of one who registers a prostitute on his Paschal lamb
phrases.notes: Signing her up as a member of his פסח is the 'payment'.

phrases.english: and that it follows Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi],
I would have established that [Mishnah]
as referring to offerings of lesser sanctity
and according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים מָמוֹן בְּעָלִים הוּא,
phrases.english: who said: offerings of lesser sanctity are the property of their owners,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דְּאוֹקְמֵיהּ רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא לְהַהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא's explanation of the אֶתְנָן משנה. The גמרא quotes that explanation itself later, in steps 7–14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אֶתְנָן משנה could be about קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, following רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, rather than about a פסח following רַבִּי.

steps.title: A person holds nothing back on his פסח animal but does on פסח money
steps.stepSummary: אַבָּיֵי explains how he understands רַבִּי. When a person consecrates a פסח animal he holds back no rights. When he sets aside money for a פסח he certainly holds some back, because he intends this from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with a פסח animal, a person does not hold anything back. With money, a person certainly does hold back. When he first sets the money aside, he sets it aside with this in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: אַבָּיֵי explains why he would not need רַבִּי's view for the משנה. In his reading, רַבִּי makes a split between the animal and the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A consecrated animal becomes fully holy, and the owner keeps no rights in it. Money set aside for a פסח is different. From the start, the person intends that he may later need it to buy into someone else's פסח, so he does not let it become fully holy. That condition is built in from the moment he separates the money (מֵעִיקָּרָא).

keyTerms.meaning: Holds back / reserves some rights for himself
A person
Money (here, money set aside for a פסח)
From the very beginning
With this intention / on this understanding
Sets aside / designates

steps.whyThisMatters: This split between animal and money is the key idea of the whole passage. Both of the next steps depend on it.

phrases.english: But with a Paschal lamb a person does not hold back [rights],
with money a person certainly holds back [rights],
for from the start, when he sets it aside,
he sets it aside with this in mind.
phrases.notes: He means it to stay usable for buying into another group's פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how אַבָּיֵי understands רַבִּי, now that the משנה has been placed with רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רַבִּי, no rights are held back in a פסח animal, but rights are held back in money set aside for a פסח.

steps.title: Applying the split to the ברייתא: the money in his hand is non-holy
steps.stepSummary: אַבָּיֵי says the ברייתא that calls the money in the owner's hand חוּלִּין is רַבִּי's view, based on the split between animal and money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this [ברייתא] is רַבִּי's view. That is why the money in his hand is חוּלִּין. A person does not hold back rights with a פסח, but he certainly does with money.
steps.whatsHappening: אַבָּיֵי now uses his split to explain the ברייתא about money received for selling a share in a פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא rules that the money the owner receives stays חוּלִּין. אַבָּיֵי says this fits רַבִּי because money is the thing a person does hold back. So the ברייתא is explained without saying that a person keeps rights in the פסח animal itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-holy, ordinary
That is in his hand
And because of this

phrases.english: And this [baraita] follows Rabbi,
and because of this the money in his hand is non-sacred,
for with a Paschal lamb a person does not hold back,
but with money a person certainly holds back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the split from step 2 to the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא calling the money חוּלִּין follows רַבִּי, because money is where a person holds back rights.

steps.title: אביי would not attribute the prostitute-payment משנה to רבי
steps.stepSummary: אַבָּיֵי concludes that he would not place the אֶתְנָן משנה with רַבִּי. In רַבִּי's view a person keeps no rights in a פסח animal, so he could not use it to pay a זוֹנָה. Only money keeps such rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that משנה, which רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא placed with רַבִּי, I would not place with רַבִּי. With a פסח a person does not hold back rights. With money he does, because when he first sets the money aside, he sets it aside with this in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: אַבָּיֵי finishes laying out his approach. He explains why, in his reading, the אֶתְנָן משנה would not follow רַבִּי and would instead be about קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, following רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי. The next step tests this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Signing up a זוֹנָה on one's פסח only works if the owner still has rights in the animal. In אַבָּיֵי's reading of רַבִּי, the owner holds back rights only in money and never in the animal. So the משנה, which assumes ownership of the animal, does not fit רַבִּי, and step 1's explanation is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: I would not establish / I would not explain it that way
Establishes (explains a source as referring to a certain case or view)
According to רַבִּי (רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא)

steps.whatToRemember: This is only אַבָּיֵי's hypothetical reading, which he would have used 'if not for' רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא. In it, no rights are held back in a פסח animal, only in money set aside for a פסח. The next step shows that the אֶתְנָן source cannot follow רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, so in step 6 אַבָּיֵי accepts רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא's reading instead.
steps.confusionAlert: The step repeats the animal-versus-money line from step 2. Here it is used for a new purpose: to show why the אֶתְנָן משנה cannot follow רַבִּי, not to explain the ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָהִיא דְּקָא מוֹקֵי לַהּ רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא כְּרַבִּי —
phrases.english: And that [Mishnah] which Rabbi Oshaya establishes as following Rabbi,
I would not establish it as following Rabbi,
for with a Paschal lamb a person does not hold back,
but with money a person does hold back.
For from the start, when he sets it aside,
he sets it aside with this in mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָהִיא דְּקָא מוֹקֵי לַהּ רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes אַבָּיֵי's approach by explaining why רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא's placement of the משנה would not work in his reading.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In אַבָּיֵי's reading, רַבִּי allows held-back rights only in money, so the אֶתְנָן משנה belongs with רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי's view on קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In אַבָּיֵי's hypothetical reading, the אֶתְנָן משנה would not follow רַבִּי, because רַבִּי allows held-back rights only in money, not in the פסח animal.

steps.title: The ברייתא cannot follow רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects his own idea of placing the ברייתא with רבי יוסי, because the same ברייתא says selling an עולה or שלמים is meaningless.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this cannot be explained as רבי יוסי's view, because the same source teaches: one who sells his עולה or his שלמים has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against his own earlier suggestion that the source follows רבי יוסי. A different line in the same ברייתא does not fit רבי יוסי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that קדשים קלים such as שלמים are the owner's property, so selling them should work. The ברייתא says selling שלמים does nothing at all. So the ברייתא cannot be רבי יוסי's view, and the רבי יוסי option falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible to explain it as following a certain opinion
Burnt-offering, which is fully given to ה׳
Peace-offering, a קדשים קלים offering
He has done nothing; the act has no legal effect

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new question from outside. אביי is checking his own earlier suggestion and admitting it does not work.

phrases.english: But this cannot be established according to Rabbi Yosei,
for it teaches in it:
and one who sells his burnt-offering and his peace-offerings
has not done anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the רבי יוסי option that אביי raised in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects placing the ברייתא with רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא says selling שלמים does nothing, but רבי יוסי treats שלמים as the owner's property.

steps.title: According to רבי, a person keeps some rights even in his פסח
steps.stepSummary: Because רבי אושעיא placed the אתנן משנה with רבי, in a case of registering a זונה on one's פסח, we learn that רבי holds a person keeps rights even in his פסח animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that רבי אושעיא explained that משנה as a case of a man who registers a זונה onto his פסח, and said it follows רבי, learn from this that רבי holds a person holds something back even in his פסח animal.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a conclusion from רבי אושעיא's explanation. רבי must hold that a person does keep some rights in his פסח animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, אביי reasoned that רבי holds no rights are kept in a פסח animal. But רבי אושעיא made the משנה work for רבי in a case where a man pays a זונה with a share in his פסח. That only works if the owner kept some rights in the animal, so this changes the picture of רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Registers someone as a member of a פסח group
A prostitute
Learn from it; a conclusion drawn from a source
A person holds back some rights when consecrating

steps.whyThisMatters: This conclusion answers how money set aside for a פסח can pass its sanctity onto a פסח animal. If the owner kept a share in the animal, that share was never fully consecrated, so sanctity can still take effect on it.

phrases.english: And now that Rabbi Oshaya established that mishna
as referring to one who registers a prostitute on his Paschal lamb,
and that it is the view of Rabbi,
learn from it that he holds
that even with his Paschal lamb a person holds something back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns away from the rejected רבי יוסי option and revises what רבי holds about a פסח animal.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי, a person keeps some rights even in his פסח animal.

steps.title: What is רבי אושעיא's teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which teaching of רבי אושעיא was just mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching of רבי אושעיא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which teaching of רבי אושעיא was just mentioned. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא quotes the משנה that רבי אושעיא explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 depended on רבי אושעיא's explanation without spelling it out. Now the גמרא goes back to the source so we can see the case for ourselves.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? A request to identify a source

phrases.english: What is that teaching of Rabbi Oshaya?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source that step 6 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which משנה רבי אושעיא explained, and how he explained it.

steps.title: The משנה about consecrated animals and birds given as a זונה's payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. Consecrated animals given as אתנן stay permitted, but non-sacred birds given as אתנן become forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: if he gave her consecrated animals as her payment, they are permitted. If he gave her non-sacred birds, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה that רבי אושעיא explained. It gives two rulings: consecrated animals are permitted, and non-sacred birds are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an animal given to a זונה as payment can never be brought as a קרבן. Here, an animal that was already consecrated does not get that status, so it stays permitted. Birds that were not consecrated do get the status and become forbidden for the מזבח. רבי אושעיא's own explanation of this משנה comes in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given to a זונה, which is forbidden for the מזבח
Animals already consecrated as קרבנות
Non-sacred birds
As we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Permitted' here means the consecrated animal can still be brought as a קרבן. It does not mean that paying a זונה is permitted.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
If he gave her consecrated animals as her payment,
these are permitted.
If he gave her non-sacred birds,
these are prohibited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by quoting the משנה that רבי אושעיא explained.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the משנה about consecrated animals and non-sacred birds given as אתנן.

steps.title: The קל וחומר that birds should be exempt from אתנן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה raises a logical argument that birds should not become אתנן, since even consecrated animals do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: For by logic it should have been permitted: consecrated animals can be disqualified by a blemish, yet the status of אתנן and מחיר does not take effect on them. Birds are not disqualified by a blemish, so is it not logical that אתנן and מחיר should not take effect on them either?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the משנה, a קל וחומר argues that birds should be exempt. This sets up the next move, where a פסוק overrides that logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Consecrated animals are sensitive, because even a blemish disqualifies them, yet they escape the אתנן status. Birds are less sensitive, because an ordinary blemish does not disqualify them. So the logic says birds should surely escape the אתנן status too, which is the opposite of the משנה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: For by logic it should have been so; introduces a קל וחומר
A physical blemish that can disqualify a קרבן
The price of a dog, which is also forbidden for the מזבח
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case

phrases.english: For it would have been logical:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אִם מוּקְדָּשִׁים שֶׁהַמּוּם פּוֹסֵל בָּהֶן
phrases.english: If consecrated animals, which a blemish disqualifies,
do not have the status of payment and price take effect on them,
then birds, which a blemish does not disqualify,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁאֵין אֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר חָל עֲלֵיהֶן?
phrases.english: is it not logical that payment and price should not take effect on them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling that birds become forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that non-sacred birds given as אתנן are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from consecrated animals, which are more sensitive yet exempt, to birds, which are less sensitive.

steps.title: The פסוק 'for any vow' includes birds
steps.stepSummary: The words 'לכל נדר' in the פסוק include birds in the אתנן prohibition, overriding the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'for any vow,' to include birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a פסוק to override the קל וחומר. The extra words 'לכל נדר' teach that birds are included in the אתנן prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic alone would have exempted birds. The extra word 'כל' in 'לכל נדר' widens the prohibition to include birds, which can be brought as a נדר. So the פסוק wins over the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; introduces a source from a פסוק
For any vow (דברים כג:יט)
To include something extra

steps.whatToRemember: In this משנה, consecrated animals given as אתנן stay permitted, but non-sacred birds become forbidden because the פסוק 'לכל נדר' includes them. רבי אושעיא's explanation of this משנה, which comes in step 14, is what showed that רבי holds a person keeps rights in his פסח.

phrases.english: The verse states: "for any vow"
to include the birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides the קל וחומר of step 9 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that non-sacred birds given as אתנן are forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'לכל נדר' in דברים כג:יט.

steps.title: A reverse argument that consecrated animals should become forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The source turns the logic around. Birds are less strict, since a מום does not disqualify them, yet they become אתנן. So קדשים, which a מום does disqualify, should surely become אתנן too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now let us argue the other way for consecrated animals. Birds are not disqualified by a blemish, yet the status of payment and price takes effect on them. Consecrated animals are disqualified by a blemish. Isn't it logical that payment and price should take effect on them too?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know birds can become אתנן, the source builds a new קל וחומר going the other direction. It argues that קדשים should become אתנן as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 argued from קדשים to birds: 'קדשים are not affected, so birds should not be either.' Now the פסוק has taught that birds are affected, so the logic can be flipped. A מום disqualifies קדשים but not birds, which shows that קדשים are more sensitive to being disqualified. If even the less sensitive birds become אתנן, the more sensitive קדשים should too.

keyTerms.meaning: From now / now that we know this
Consecrated animals set aside for the בית המקדש
A physical blemish that disqualifies an animal from being a קרבן
The 'price of a dog': money from selling a dog, which is also forbidden for קרבנות
'Is it not logical?' The formula that sets up a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Now, here is a kal vachomer about consecrated animals:

phrases.aramaic: מָה עוֹפוֹת שֶׁאֵין הַמּוּם פּוֹסֵל בָּהֶן
phrases.english: Just as birds, which a blemish does not disqualify,
still get the status of a prostitute's payment and a dog's price,
phrases.notes: We learned this from 'לכל נדר' in step 10.

phrases.english: then consecrated animals, which a blemish does disqualify,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁאֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר חָל עֲלֵיהֶן?
phrases.english: is it not logical that payment and price should take effect on them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 10 (birds become אתנן) to build a reverse קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 8 that קדשים given as אתנן stay permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מום makes קדשים more easily disqualified than birds. If birds become אתנן, then קדשים should become אתנן all the more.

steps.title: The word 'vow' excludes animals that were already vowed
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'לכל נדר', meaning 'for any vow'. This excludes something that has already been vowed. So קדשים cannot become אתנן, and the reverse קל וחומר is rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'for any vow.' This excludes something that was already vowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The source answers the reverse קל וחומר with the פסוק. Something already vowed to הקדש does not become אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition is that one may not bring אתנן 'for any vow', meaning to fulfill a future vow. An animal that is already consecrated has already been vowed. So the פסוק itself leaves it out, and the logical argument cannot override the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Excluding, except for
Something already vowed or consecrated
A vow, such as a promise to bring a קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: The same words 'לכל נדר' do two jobs. They include birds in the אתנן prohibition (step 10), and they exclude animals that are already consecrated (this step).

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'for any vow,'
which excludes something already vowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reverse קל וחומר of step 11 using a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That consecrated animals do not become אתנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'לכל נדר' in דברים כג:יט, read as excluding what is already vowed

steps.title: Why was a verse needed? A person cannot forbid what is not his
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the source needed a פסוק to stop קדשים from becoming אתנן. But that should be obvious, because a person cannot forbid something that does not belong to him, and קדשים belong to הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the reason is only that the Torah wrote 'vow.' Without that, I would have said the prohibition of a prostitute's payment does take effect on consecrated animals. But a person cannot forbid something that is not his!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source for needing a פסוק at all. Basic logic should already tell us that קדשים cannot become אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source implies that without the word 'נדר', קדשים would become אתנן. But once an animal is consecrated, it belongs to הקדש and not to the person. A person cannot place an איסור on property that is not his, so the פסוק seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason; here it means 'the only reason is'
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
I would have thought; the initial assumption

keyTerms.term: אֵין אָדָם אוֹסֵר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A person cannot make forbidden something that does not belong to him

phrases.english: But the only reason is that the Torah wrote 'vow';
if not for that, I would have said
that the prohibition of a prostitute's payment takes effect on consecrated animals.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אֵין אָדָם אוֹסֵר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ!
phrases.english: But a person cannot forbid something that is not his!
phrases.notes: Consecrated animals belong to הקדש, not to the person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption behind step 12: that without the פסוק, קדשים would become אתנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source's need for the word 'נדר' to exclude קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קדשים belong to הקדש, and a person cannot forbid what is not his, so no פסוק should be needed to exclude them.

steps.title: The case is giving a זונה a share in one's פסח, following רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא explains the case. A man pays a זונה by registering her on his קרבן פסח. This follows רבי, who holds that a person keeps ownership rights in his פסח. So without the פסוק, the animal could have become אתנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: The case is one who registers a prostitute on his Paschal lamb, and this follows the view of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא answers the challenge. He sets the case in a situation where the person still has rights in the consecrated animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person has no rights in קדשים. But according to רבי, an owner still has a real share in his פסח, which he can give to others. Since it is partly 'his', we might have thought he can make it אתנן. That is why the פסוק was needed to exclude it.

keyTerms.meaning: Registers someone as a participant in a קרבן פסח
A prostitute
His קרבן פסח
This follows the view of רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same statement of רבי אושעיא already mentioned in step 6. The גמרא is now quoting it in its full original context. It is not a new opinion.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
The case is one who registers a prostitute on his Paschal lamb,
and this follows the view of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (אוקימתא) plus attributing the source to a particular תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קדשים fully belong to הקדש, so a פסוק to exclude them is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי's view, a person keeps rights in his פסח, so we might have thought he can make it אתנן. The פסוק teaches that he cannot.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is where step 6's conclusion comes from: רבי holds that a person has ownership rights in his פסח.

steps.title: Which teaching of רבי is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see that רבי holds a person has rights in his פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the teaching of רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי's view. This sets up the next step, which quotes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא relied on רבי's opinion without quoting it. The גמרא wants the actual source showing that an owner can give shares in his פסח to others.

keyTerms.meaning: What?
רבי יהודה הנשיא, compiler of the משנה

phrases.english: What is this teaching of Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view of רבי cited in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text where רבי shows that a person has rights in his פסח

steps.title: A poor man may support himself from his פסח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads the פסוק 'אם ימעט הבית מהיות משה' as allowing a poor man to support himself from his lamb. He sells shares in it for money, but only to pay for food, not for other purchases.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'If the household be too little for a lamb' means: sustain him from the lamb. This applies when he lacks enough for food, but not when he lacks enough for other purchases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the ברייתא that contains רבי's view. This first clause is the opinion of the תנא קמא: a poor owner may sell portions of his פסח, but only to cover his food needs. רבי's own view comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'מהיות' as 'החייהו', meaning 'keep him alive' from the lamb. If the owner can take money for shares in his פסח, he clearly still has rights in it. This permission is limited to buying food for the יום טוב, not other items.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
The household is too little, read here as 'too poor'
Sustain him, keep him alive
Enough means for food
A purchase of other items

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא lets a poor owner sell shares in his פסח only to pay for food. רבי goes further in the next step, and his reason (שעל מנת כן הקדישו ישראל את פסחיהן) is the source for רבי אושעיא's claim that an owner keeps rights in his פסח.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
'If the household be too little for a lamb' (Shemos 12:4),
means: sustain him from the lamb.
phrases.notes: He sells shares in his פסח for money.

phrases.english: This applies when he lacks enough to eat,
but not when he lacks enough for other purchases.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא אִם יִמְעַט הַבַּיִת מִהְיוֹת מִשֶּׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 15 by quoting רבי's ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי's ברייתא: a poor owner may support himself from his פסח by selling shares in it, but only for food.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A person has ownership rights in his פסח, which explains רבי אושעיא's case of registering a זונה on it.

steps.title: רבי allows selling shares even for other purchases
steps.stepSummary: רבי says a poor man may register others on his פסח and חגיגה even to buy other things. The money is חולין, because Jews consecrate their פסח on that condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: even for buying things. If he has no money, he may sign another person onto his פסח and his חגיגה. The money he receives is not holy, because Jews consecrate their פסח animals on exactly this condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with רבי's opinion. This is the actual proof for the question in step 15, showing that רבי holds a person keeps rights in his פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allowed using the money only for food. רבי goes further and allows it for other purchases too, and he rules the money is plain חולין. He explains that every Jew consecrates his פסח with this condition built in, so the owner keeps a real money right in it. That retained right is exactly what רבי אושעיא needed in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: enough money to make a purchase (beyond just food)
registers / signs someone onto a קרבן
the festival peace-offering brought along with the פסח
non-holy, ordinary money
on this condition

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' here means רבי יהודה הנשיא. He is a specific person, not 'a rabbi' in general.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line proves that, according to רבי, a person keeps a money right in his פסח. That is why a פסוק was needed to stop a פסח from becoming אתנן.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: even for the means of a purchase,
for if he does not have —
he registers another person with him
on his Paschal lamb and on his festival offering,
and the money in his hand is non-sacred,
for it is on this condition
that Israel consecrated their Paschal lambs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 16 by adding רבי's broader view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we see that רבי holds a person has rights in his פסח?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי rules the money from registering others is חולין and may be used even for other purchases, because Jews consecrate their פסח on that condition.
steps.raayaObject: רבי holds a person keeps ownership rights in his פסח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: 'ומעות שבידו חולין, שעל מנת כן הקדישו ישראל את פסחיהן'.

steps.title: First view: everyone allows wood, the argument is about מצה and מרור
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רבי זירא disagree on the scope of the מחלוקת. One says all agree the money may buy wood to roast the פסח, since that counts like the פסח itself. The argument is only about מצה and מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רבי זירא: one said, about wood for roasting the פסח, everyone agrees. Since it is a preparation of the פסח, it is like the פסח itself. Where they argue is about מצה and מרור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion. Two אמוראים try to pin down exactly where רבי and the רבנן disagree, and here is the first view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood is needed to roast the פסח, so it counts as part of the פסח itself. That is why even the רבנן allow the money to be spent on it. The real argument is about money spent on מצה and מרור, and the next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: wood for roasting it (the פסח)
everyone agrees
a preparation of the פסח
it is like the פסח itself
where they do argue

phrases.english: Rabba and Rabbi Zeira — one said:
regarding wood for roasting it,
everyone agrees,
since it is a preparation of the Paschal lamb —
it is like the Paschal lamb itself.
Where they argue is about matza and bitter herbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא is fully quoted, the אמוראים define where רבי and the רבנן actually disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone allows the money for wood to roast the פסח. The מחלוקת is about מצה and מרור.

steps.title: Reasoning of the first view: separate eating or part of the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן see מצה and מרור as a separate eating. רבי sees them as what makes the פסח eaten properly, so they count like the פסח itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that this is a different eating. רבי holds that since it makes the פסח eaten properly, it is like the פסח itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The first view now explains the reasoning of each side in the argument over מצה and מרור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, מצה and מרור are their own מצוות of eating, separate from the פסח, so the money cannot go to them. For רבי, the פסח is supposed to be eaten with them, so they serve the פסח and count like it.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages hold
a different, separate eating
what makes it proper / enables it

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: הָא אֲכִילָה אַחֲרִיתִי הִיא.
phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: this is a different eating.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּהֶכְשֵׁירוֹ דְפֶסַח הוּא —
phrases.english: And Rabbi holds: since it is what makes the Paschal lamb proper —
it is like the Paschal lamb itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: הָא אֲכִילָה אַחֲרִיתִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the argument defined in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן treat מצה and מרור as a separate eating. רבי treats them as part of the פסח.

steps.title: Second view: everyone allows מצה and מרור, the argument is about clothing
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says everyone allows the money for מצה and מרור, because the פסוק links them to eating the פסח. The argument is about buying a shirt or a cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: about מצה and מרור, everyone also agrees, as it is written, 'with מצות and bitter herbs they shall eat it.' Since they enable the פסח, they are like the פסח. Where they argue is about buying a shirt or a cloak with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The second אמורא gives a different picture. He moves the agreement further out and puts the argument somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק says to eat the פסח 'על מצות ומרורים', מצה and מרור are tied to the פסח. So even the רבנן allow the money for them. The argument is now only about personal needs like clothing, which have nothing to do with the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is written
with מצות and bitter herbs they shall eat it (במדבר ט:יא)
things that enable / make proper
a shirt
a cloak / outer garment

phrases.english: And one said: regarding matza and bitter herbs also,
everyone agrees,
as it is written: 'With matzot and bitter herbs they shall eat it,'
for since they are enablers of the Paschal lamb —
they are like the Paschal lamb.
Where they argue is to buy a shirt with it,
to buy a cloak with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: בְּמַצָּה וּמָרוֹר נָמֵי כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing definition of the מחלוקת, against the first view in steps 18-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone allows the money for מצה and מרור. The מחלוקת is about clothing.

steps.title: Reasoning of the second view: two readings of מהיות משה
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read 'מהיות משה' as 'keep the lamb going,' so the money is only for the lamb's needs. רבי reads it as 'keep yourself going from the lamb,' so the money is for all of your needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that the Torah said 'מהיות משה', meaning 'keep the lamb alive.' רבי holds it means 'keep yourself alive from the lamb.'
steps.whatsHappening: The second view explains that the whole argument comes from two ways of reading the פסוק 'מהיות משה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the money may only be spent on what the lamb needs, such as wood, מצה and מרור. For רבי, the man may support himself from the lamb, so even clothing is allowed. This fits רבי's view in step 17 that the owner keeps real rights in his פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'from being for a lamb' (שמות יב:ד)
the Torah (literally 'the Merciful One')
keep the lamb going (spend only on its needs)
keep yourself going from the lamb

steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים agree that רבי is more lenient than the רבנן. They only argue about where the line falls: מצה and מרור, or clothing. In the second view, the argument depends on reading 'מהיות משה' as 'for the lamb' or 'from the lamb.'
steps.confusionAlert: The Hebrew letter מ in 'משה' is read two ways. The רבנן take it as 'for the lamb.' רבי takes it as 'from the lamb,' meaning you may live off of it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: the Torah said 'miheyot miseh,'
meaning: sustain the lamb,
and Rabbi holds: sustain yourself from the lamb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the textual basis for the clothing argument defined in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן read 'מהיות משה' as 'sustain the lamb.' רבי reads it as 'sustain yourself from the lamb.'

steps.title: Recalling אביי's view that a פסח is fully consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back אביי's earlier statement. He said that if not for רבי אושעיא's reading, he would have explained the earlier teaching as speaking about קדשים קלים according to רבי יוסי הגלילי. With a פסח, however, nobody holds back any part from הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי, who said: 'If רבי אושעיא had not explained that teaching as a case of someone who registers a זונה on his פסח, following רבי, I would have explained it as speaking about קדשים קלים, following רבי יוסי הגלילי. He says קדשים קלים still belong to the owners. But with a פסח, a person does not hold anything back.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes אביי's earlier statement so it can challenge it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי held that קדשים קלים still count as the owner's property, but a פסח does not, because people consecrate it completely. That claim suggests that even רבי sees the פסח as fully הקדש. The next step will test this against רבי's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: He established it, meaning he explained which case the teaching is talking about
One who registers someone as a partner on his offering
Offerings of lesser holiness
Property of the owners
A person does not leave anything over (unconsecrated)

phrases.english: And according to Abaye, who said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּאוֹקְמַהּ רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא לְהַהִיא
phrases.english: If Rabbi Oshaya had not established that (teaching)
as speaking of one who registers a prostitute on his Paschal lamb
and that it follows Rebbi,
we would have established it as speaking of offerings of lesser holiness
and following Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who said: offerings of lesser holiness are the property of their owners,
but with a Paschal lamb, a person does not hold anything back —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the רבה and רבי זירא argument back to רבי's ruling in step 17, setting up a challenge to אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אביי, a פסח is fully consecrated, unlike קדשים קלים, which per רבי יוסי הגלילי remain the owner's property.

steps.title: רבי's own words seem to say the פסח is not fully consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explicitly quotes רבי: 'on this condition Jews consecrate their פסח.' That sounds like the פסח is consecrated only partly, against אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches explicitly: 'For on this condition Jews consecrated their פסח'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי using the exact words of רבי quoted in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said the פסח itself was consecrated with a condition attached. If so, it was not consecrated completely, and part of its value stays with the owner. That contradicts אביי's claim that nobody holds back anything from a פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches explicitly
On this condition
They consecrated

phrases.english: But it teaches explicitly:

phrases.aramaic: ״שֶׁעַל מְנָת כֵּן הִקְדִּישׁוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת פִּסְחֵיהֶן״?
phrases.english: "For on this condition the Jewish people consecrated their Paschal lambs"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's statement quoted in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that a person does not hold back any part of his פסח from הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי's wording says the animal itself was consecrated with a condition, so it was not consecrated completely.

steps.title: Changing the wording: the condition was on the money, not the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the ברייתא's wording to 'on this condition Jews consecrated the money of their פסח.' The condition applies to the money, so the animal itself can still be fully consecrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'For on this condition Jews consecrated the money of their פסח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by adjusting one word in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition was never about the animal. It was about the money that people pay when they register on someone's פסח, which stays חולין. So the animal can still be fully הקדש, and אביי's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way instead)
The money of their Paschal lambs

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say רבי changed his ruling. The money is still חולין and may be used freely. Only the reason shifts: the condition is placed on the money, not on the animal's holiness.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the פסח animal is fully consecrated. רבי's condition applies only to the money paid by those who register on it.

phrases.english: Say:
For on this condition the Jewish people consecrated
the money of their Paschal lambs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי said the animal itself was consecrated with a condition, which would contradict אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition applies only to the money for the פסח. The animal is fully consecrated, as אביי said.

steps.title: Slaughtering the פסח for a זב who is finishing his purification
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. For a זב who saw two discharges, we may slaughter the פסח on his seventh clean day. For one who saw three, we slaughter on his eighth day, the day he brings his offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A זב who saw two discharges: we slaughter the פסח for him on his seventh day. If he saw three: we slaughter for him on his eighth day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with people who are still impure on ערב פסח but will be pure by nightfall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב who saw two discharges needs seven clean days and then immersion, so he becomes pure that evening and can eat the פסח at night. A זב who saw three discharges must also bring an offering on the eighth day. We assume he will bring it, so we may slaughter the פסח for him that day.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
A man impure because of an unusual bodily discharge
Sightings (instances of discharge)
We slaughter (the פסח) on his behalf

steps.whyThisMatters: A person may be included in a פסח even while still impure at the time of slaughter, as long as he will be pure in time to eat it at night.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A zav who saw two sightings (of discharge) —
we slaughter (the Paschal lamb) on his behalf on the seventh (day).
If he saw three —
we slaughter on his behalf on his eighth (day).
phrases.notes: This is the day he brings his purification offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה, unrelated to the money discussion before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We may slaughter the פסח for a זב on the last day of his purification: the seventh day if he saw two discharges, the eighth if he saw three.

steps.title: Slaughtering the פסח for a שומרת יום כנגד יום
steps.stepSummary: For a שומרת יום כנגד יום who saw blood on one day, we slaughter the פסח for her on her second day. If she saw blood on two days, we slaughter on the third day.
steps.simpleTranslation: A שומרת יום כנגד יום: we slaughter for her on her second day. If she saw blood for two days: we slaughter for her on the third day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a similar rule for a woman with a minor discharge outside her regular cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She waits one clean day after her last discharge and immerses on that day. If she saw blood on one day, that clean day is her second day. If she saw blood on two days, it is her third day. We slaughter for her on that day, even though she could still see more blood later.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who keeps watch one clean day for each day of discharge
She saw (a discharge)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lets us slaughter the פסח for someone who is still finishing purification, as long as the purification is due to be complete that day.

phrases.english: A woman who keeps watch a day for a day —
we slaughter on her behalf on her second (day),
if she saw (discharge on) two days —
we slaughter on her behalf on the third (day).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a parallel case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We may slaughter the פסח for a שומרת יום כנגד יום on her clean day: the second day after one day of discharge, the third day after two.

steps.title: A זבה gets her קרבן פסח on the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by ruling that for a זבה, the פסח is slaughtered on her eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for a זבה, we slaughter the פסח for her on the eighth day.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It says a זבה is treated like a זב who saw three times, so her פסח is slaughtered on her eighth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זבה is a woman who saw blood on three days in a row outside her normal time. Like a זב who saw three times, she counts seven clean days, immerses, and brings an offering on the eighth day. So the משנה lets the פסח be slaughtered for her on that eighth day, just as it did for the זב in Step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who saw blood on three days in a row outside her normal time. She needs seven clean days and an offering.
The eighth day, when she brings her offering.
For her, on her behalf

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's full list: a זב who saw twice gets the פסח on day 7. A זב who saw three times, and a זבה, get it on day 8. A שומרת יום כנגד יום gets it on day 2 or day 3.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this זבה with the שומרת יום כנגד יום in the previous step. The שומרת יום only saw on one or two days and needs just one clean day. A זבה saw on three days and needs seven clean days plus an offering.

phrases.english: And a woman who is a zava —
phrases.notes: She saw blood on three days in a row, so she is a full זבה.

phrases.english: we slaughter for her on the eighth day.
phrases.notes: This is the day she brings her offering, like the זב who saw three times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's list of people who are partway through purification. It matches the זבה to the זב who saw three times.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a זבה, the פסח is slaughtered on her eighth day, the day of her offering.

steps.title: רב: we may slaughter for a טבול יום and for a מחוסר כפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רב יהודה quoting רב. We may slaughter the פסח and sprinkle its blood for a טבול יום and for a מחוסר כפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: We slaughter the פסח and sprinkle its blood for a טבול יום, and for a מחוסר כפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by bringing a rule from רב. Someone who is almost finished with his purification may still have the פסח slaughtered and its blood sprinkled for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבול יום has already gone to the מקוה, but he only becomes fully טהור when night comes. A מחוסר כפורים has finished everything except bringing his offering. רב says neither one is held back from the פסח. By nighttime, when the פסח is eaten, each of them will be able to eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
We sprinkle the blood of the offering on the מזבח
Someone who has gone to the מקוה today. He becomes fully טהור only at nightfall.
Someone who has finished becoming טהור but still needs to bring his atonement offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains the logic behind the משנה. The day-8 cases in the משנה are exactly people who are a מחוסר כפורים, and רב says the פסח may still be slaughtered for them.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line. רב יהודה is reporting his teacher רב.

phrases.english: We slaughter and sprinkle the blood for one who immersed today,
phrases.notes: He will be fully טהור by night, when the פסח is eaten.

phrases.english: and for one who still lacks his atonement offering,
phrases.notes: For example, a זב on his eighth day before he has brought his offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שׁוֹחֲטִין וְזוֹרְקִין עַל טְבוּל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה is done, and the גמרא begins. It brings an אמורא's general rule about people who are partway through purification.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסח may be slaughtered, and its blood sprinkled, for a טבול יום and for a מחוסר כפורים.
